Sessions / Session 04 Day 2

Session 04 — Day 2: La Scelta

The first full open day. Registration at the Mercatura bridge. The city belongs to the party — throw one or two hooks in the first hour to pull players who want direction; leave the rest to be found. Don’t throw all five at once.

Dawn — What Changed Overnight

ThreadState at dawn
BrancaStill in the shrine. Upright, awake, booklet on her knee. She has not moved. The font is still breathing.
FestivalLa Scelta — registration desks open. Marks are notified this morning. Cloth and masks go up on every major facade.
RaidDay 2 of prep. Route testing underway. Handlers walking Le Paludi and Bridge routes at pace, timing transfers. Slaad pre-positioning begins.
ShipSem has paint stripped on the port quarter. Day 2 of ~5.
Red LadyCommission clock: 7–9 days. Diving apparatus rental order placed yesterday.

Hooks — Morning

SituationHook (comes to them)Lands on
Pearl SummonsBranca will not leave the shrine (see below) — nudge on long rest attemptDelmar
Warren & NonaThe sending stone speaks: Nona names the favorPerrin
Sewer GrungA private recognition beat: the Velo Grung watching the crowd “wrong”Jean-Claude
Red LadyA chandler mention, or Kyzil names the money to CrissdalynnDelmar / Crissdalynn
BeffaRegistration desk is live; a Beffa team eyes a PCAny
DM Note

Let the party choose which direction to pull. Run situations in whatever order they engage them. Every beat below is self-contained.

Beffa Registration

Optional — the most fun; background if skipped.

Read Aloud

The Mercatura bridge has become a registration desk. A woman with ink-stained fingers and the patience of a saint sits behind a ledger that already has three crossed-out team names on this page alone. Behind her, someone’s mask has fallen off mid-argument and rolled under the desk. She retrieves it without looking up. “Team name, mark, category, stake. If you say ‘The Masked Avengers’ I am crossing you out before you finish.”

The toy: if they register, get the table choosing — team name, mark, category, symbol, stake. Standard entry is 25 gp; Legendary-scale is 50 gp. Scoring: Craft 10, Surprise 5, Recovery 5, out of 20. Loud, dumb, theirs.

Giacomo Moretti has signed the Accord for twenty years and has never been successfully pranked. The committee finds this professionally embarrassing. He is listed as a valid mark.

Hook: a Beffa team picks a PC as their mark in the first hour — the Wrong Mark drop (fish oil from a balcony, a wrong name on a real permit; Street Encounters #1).

If ignored: the Beffa runs without them — cloth in the streets, nervous marks, daily results at sundown. Nothing closes; it’s ambient texture and a five-day clock.

The Shrine — Pearl Summons

Delmar (primary), Crissdalynn (was there when Branca first found him). Revelation / horror set-piece.

This is a fixed dramatic beat, not a negotiation. The offer is unacceptable by design; the refusal is expected; the point is the demonstration. Run it as scripted and let the silence between boxes work.

Arrival

Read Aloud

The Waveservant Shrine is a low, tide-stained vault off a Mercatura canal. The font behind the bench holds a hand’s depth of seawater that will not lie flat — it rises and falls, slow, like something breathing under it. Branca is exactly where she sat down: upright, awake, salt-white hair pulled back hard, the little leather tide-table booklet open on her knee. “So,” she says, bright and clipped, the warmth of someone rescheduling a missed meeting. “You came. Good. We have an appointment.”

NPC — Branca: corporate cult executive assistant — bubbly, efficient, too much eye contact; opens “So!”, closes “Does that work for you?”, checks the booklet mid-sentence as if it settles every objection. She believes making divine horror pleasant is a kindness. She is the soft instrument; what comes through her is not.

The Possession

Branca stops mid-sentence. Her eyes roll back to white. The voice is not hers.

Read Aloud

Branca’s eyes roll white. When she speaks it is not her voice — it is the sea given a throat, cold and enormous and patient. “FISK. You carry what is Mine. Go down to the wreck. Bring Me the Pearl. Return it to My shrine — and I will grant you the one mercy you have earned: a swift death, and the souls you stole brought home to Me. This is My grace. Accept it.”

The demand (plainly): retrieve the Pearl of Souls from the Red Lady wreck at the Drowned Maw and return it to a shrine of Umberlee. The “reward” is Delmar’s own death and the surrender of the souls he carries. A death sentence dressed as salvation. He will refuse — by design.

DM Note

This brushes Delmar’s secret. The party hears that he

carries souls Umberlee claims and that there’s a Pearl to retrieve. They need not learn the five captains / Vel Orn story — keep Her words to “what is Mine” and “the souls you stole.” Only Delmar’s player knows he carries voices.

The Wrath

The instant Delmar refuses:

Read Aloud

The refusal is barely out of your mouth before the light goes wrong. Thunder walks across a sky that was clear a breath ago; the canal shivers in its channel. The thing wearing Branca

roars — and then, almost offhand, it takes her head in her own two hands and snaps her neck. The body folds. The shrine goes silent. Branca lies on the wet stone, not breathing.

Hold the silence. Then —

The Return

Read Aloud

Mist gathers off the canal — too fast, too deliberate — and curls in around the fallen woman like a tide coming home. Branca’s chest heaves. She drags in one enormous, gasping breath, sits up, blinks the white from her eyes, finds the booklet, smooths her robe, and looks up with that same bright warmth, as if nothing happened. “I hope,” she says, “you understand my lady Umberlee’s power. And her grace.”

Insight — After the Revival

DC 12 (no advantage from prior knowledge; this is emotional, not logical). Fail: reads as shock; the depth doesn’t register. Success: Branca means it completely — she experienced her own murder as a privilege and is not performing.

That is the horror. Crit success: Branca has been through this before. Not once. Her faith is forged, not learned — and the thing that spoke through her left a trace of salt on the air that is not fading.

The bind: the only way to satisfy the goddess is to die for her, so Delmar has to find a third answer — and the Pearl she wants is inside the Red Lady — exactly what the salvage commission is racing for. Demand and money pull at the same wreck from opposite directions.

Warren & Nona — The Favor Named

Perrin (primary, family), Delmar (ship silhouette). Social / logistics.

Perrin already visited Nona in Session 03 — apologized, heard about the Vestra, agreed to the favor unconditionally, and left with the sending stone. Two linked problems remain. (a) The Uncertainty still reads as a Crown cutter to anyone who knows cutters — paint won’t fix a silhouette. Carpenters’ Slip won’t take a cold approach; she needs a Warren introduction, which runs through Nona. (b) Nona is ready to name the favor and use the sending stone to do it.

DM Note

When Perrin meets with Nona (whenever that happens), she drops one line unprompted after the favor is named: “Your ship reads wrong. I know a woman at the Slip — Savia. Tell her I sent you.” This wires the ship-repair thread through Nona rather than requiring the party to deduce the connection.

The Hook — The Stone Speaks

Nona uses the sending stone this morning. One sentence, flat, unhurried.

Read Aloud

The stone warms in Perrin’s pocket. Nona’s voice, close as a whisper, no greeting: “Come back. Bring the blue one.”

DM Note

The stone is a one-sentence channel. Nona will not explain via stone — she needs Perrin at her table. If he comes, she feeds him first, names the favor second. She already knows about the Vestra; that grief is held, not absent. Today is business.

NPC — Nona Black-Jaw (page): feeds you first, names what you owe second — as accounting, not threat. She knows the Vestra is gone (quietly grieving the men and the money while planning the response).

The Favor

DM Note

Nona’s favor (canon). Word reached Nona that Perrin came in with a crew including a blue Grung in a beret and moustache (Jean-Claude). She reads it as luck. She’s had reports she’d normally dismiss as impossible this far north — Grung moving in the old Warren tunnels that intersect the Calveno sewers — and wants them confirmed or dismissed. Who better to hunt Grung than a Grung. The ask: send JC (with whoever he wants) into the tunnels to confirm. This is the door into the raid — those sewer Grung are Simone’s extraction crews; this and the handler thread are the same investigation from two ends.

The Rattle — Demonstration

If the party is inside the Warren during the visit, Nona has a reason to show them what the community can do. A Dravosi factor’s runner is spotted at the Le Paludi canal edge — not a raid, but close enough to protocol that someone triggers the drill.

Read Aloud

A pan strikes somewhere behind the kitchen wall. One beat, two, three — a rhythm, not music. Before the echo dies another pan picks it up, farther away, deeper in the stone. Then another. Within the space of a held breath the sound is everywhere — rising through vents, ringing off pipe, carried by hands you cannot see. The kitchen stops. Nona sets down her spoon.

Read Aloud

Movement. Not panic — purpose. A Rattkin woman in a flour-dusted apron crosses behind Nona and pulls a short blade from behind a cutting board. An old Rattkin by the door slides a bar into a bracket that was not visible a moment ago. A child — nine, maybe ten — darts past Perrin’s ankles and vanishes into a gap in the wall no wider than a fist. From the corridor beyond, the sound of a heavy object being dragged across stone. The whole Warren is moving, and it has been moving since the first pan struck.

Let the party sit inside this for a moment. Then —

Read Aloud

Two taps. Quick, sharp, final. The sound dies. The bar comes off the door. The blade goes back behind the cutting board. The child reappears from a different gap than the one he entered. Nona picks up her spoon. “Thirty seconds,” she says. “We have been doing this since before your mother was born.”

DM Note

This is not a set-piece. This is Nona showing the party — specifically Perrin — what the Warren is and what she built. The Rattle converts surprise into readiness across the entire community in half a minute. The party should understand that this district cannot be taken by stealth. The cost of the demonstration: the party now knows the Warren’s alarm system. Nona trusts Perrin enough to show him. She trusts his crew because he brought them.

The Ship Problem

NPC — Savia Brentino (Carpenters’ Slip): dry, unhurried, says the hard thing once and lets it sit. Wants: a Warren introduction before she’ll deal — three ships tried cold this month and are on her list. Reveals (flatly, at the end): “She’ll still read as a cutter to anyone who knows cutters. That’s not a paint problem.”

Terms: 220 gp + 5 city days + one unassigned Tangle favour. The bow registry plate is the party’s call.

Insight — On Savia

DC 13. Fail: she reads as a dead end, the silhouette stays unsolved. Success: she isn’t hostile, she’s screening; an introduction flips her. Crit success: the three ships she turned away this month were all asking the wrong questions. Her refusal is professional, not personal — she knows who she can trust and is waiting for proof.

If ignored: the Savia introduction requires a return visit to Nona. The silhouette stays live and the Crown clock keeps ticking; every unpapered day is a day the ship is easier to recognize.

First Handler Beat — Jean-Claude

JC only. Private. One recognition beat — do not announce to the table.

DM Note

As soon as JC enters any crowd scene — Mercatura, Bridge, Velo square — slide his player a written note or whisper the read-aloud below. Do not announce to the table. If his player doesn’t bite, don’t push — mark the lane as confirmed for the raid and move on. The beat fires once; repeating it turns a private moment into a quest marker.

Crowd positioning. A Grung at the Bridge or Velo stands in the one position that gives sightlines to three exits without appearing to watch any. Jean-Claude has stood in that position. It is trained, not instinctive.

Read Aloud

A blue-caste Grung stands at the edge of a Velo square, watching a street performer. He is not enjoying it. He is watching how the crowd

moves when the performer makes a scene — where people turn, where the gaps open, how long a knot of onlookers takes to dissolve.

If JC acts: this is observation, not combat. The Velo Grung is polite, says he’s here for the festival. Karath accent, not Veth. No trade goods, no festival registration, no declared purpose for being this far west. If JC pushes harder, the Grung excuses himself and leaves — quickly, efficiently, without running. He files a report. JC’s face enters the handler network.

If JC reports to the party: the party now has one confirmed handler sighting. No proof, no combat, no confirmation of the raid — just dread that Jean-Claude can name and no one else can.

If ignored: the handler completes his route assessment. One more lane is locked for the raid.

Red Lady — First Threads

Delmar (primary), Crissdalynn (Kyzil sub-beat). Investigation / social.

Two ways this surfaces today:

Through city gossip (any PC asking about salvage, the Maw, or unusual money):

Read Aloud

A chandler lowers his voice without being asked. “You’re not the first to ask about Maw salvage this month. There’s money moving. Serious money — three buyers, or one buyer with three hands, nobody’s sure. And they’re not advertising a target.”

Investigation / Gather Info — Salvage Talk

DC 12 (DC 8 if Delmar asks specifically about Maw salvage gear). Fail: only the rumour of “money moving.” Success (two of three): hired diving apparatus, compressed-air bladders, a sealed chart package a courier wouldn’t hand off. Crit success: all three, plus the name “Zusto” — a Bridge broker handling the supply chain.

Through Kyzil (Crissdalynn only):

Kyzil knows what the party doesn’t — Crissdalynn’s original ship went down to “a foul wind from the south.” If she pulls on Red Lady traces with Kyzil present, he can set that phrase against the Maw rumours. Reveal one layer at most — he’s grief held under discipline; his instinct is to protect her, not dump lore.

DM Note

Don’t force the Kyzil reveal. If Crissdalynn asks about the Maw, wrecks, or her past in his presence, he gives one careful sentence. If she doesn’t today, he holds it — but he does not hold it forever. If the party discusses salvage, wrecks, or Maw money in Kyzil’s earshot on any later day, he volunteers one guarded sentence: “I should tell you something about that wreck.” His protection is timing, not permanent silence.

If ignored: the commission clock ticks. One more day of gear sourcing, crew assembly, and chart preparation. Savia mentions the suspicious enquiries to anyone who earns her trust — but only once.

Moustache Craftsman — JC Roleplay Beat

Optional. Drop if JC walks through the Velo Quarter.

Read Aloud

A narrow booth between a wig maker and a vendor of theatrical smoke. The boards are covered in prosthetics, false beards, and a row of spectacles the man inside is not wearing. The spirit gum smell reaches you from three feet away. He has not looked up.

Giacinto — gnome, late sixties, reading glasses on forehead, permanently smelling of spirit gum. Spots JC’s moustache as his own work. Points to the inner-edge cut on the right corner: “That’s one of mine. Who are you wearing it for?”

He explains that the moustache-and-beret combination reads as “performer” — which, in a festival city, is its own kind of invisible. “Nobody looks twice at a performer. Don’t change anything.” He begins re-sealing the edges before anyone agrees to it.

Day Close — What Moves Overnight

ThreadOvernight movement
BrancaIf the Pearl Summons fired: Branca leaves the shrine, her appointment complete. If Delmar still hasn’t gone: she is in the shrine at dawn, same position, for the third consecutive dawn.
RaidDay 2 complete. Route testing finished — handlers know the transfer times for all five sewer access points. Slaad pre-positioning continues.
NonaIf the party answered the stone: the favor is named; JC’s tunnel job is on the table. If Perrin ignored the stone: Nona waits one more day, then sends a runner directly.
Red LadyCommission clock: 6–8 days. Crew contacts in two ports have been confirmed. A sealed chart package was delivered to the Bridge exchange.
ShipDay 2 of ~5. Port-quarter repaint underway. Sem needs a decision on the registry plate by Day 4.
BeffaLa Scelta complete. Marks have been notified. La Finestra opens at dawn — the three-day execution window begins.
